Electric Tugboats Get L.A. Audition

Plus: U.S. import prices increase for a third straight month; robotics startup Genesis AI raises $500 million to help fund large-scale training

By

Tugboats that maneuver containerships through America’s busiest ports are starting to go electric. California -based Curtin Maritime is developing eight battery-powered tugs in partnership with marine-technology startup Arc, part of a push to replace conventional diesel engines with electric propulsion.

The Dow Jones Risk Journal’s Perry Cleveland-Peck writes that the first vessel is undergoing sea trials with the U.S. Coast Guard ahead of planned delivery later this month. It will be the first fully electric tug operating at the Port of Los Angeles. Eight tugboats would represent around a third of the current fleet operating in both the Port of L.A. and the Port of Long Beach.
